title: Delete some of your offers: why fewer products and one price per offer sell more
summary: Justin argues that too many offers and price tiers cause decision fatigue and quietly kill sales. He recommends one course, one community and one service, each with a single price, so customers only choose how they want to "do it": alone, with others, or done for them.

principles.text: Too many options cause decision fatigue, and people then choose nothing.
principles.quote: Decision fatigue happens when too many options wear out your brain, making it difficult to actually make a choice.

principles.text: Give each course a single price instead of tiers or bundles.
principles.quote: And this is exactly why each of the courses I offer has one price. That's it.

principles.text: Sell one service tailored to common client needs: take it or leave it.
principles.quote: When I offered consulting back in the day, I had one offer tailored to the most common needs of my clients. Take it or leave it.

principles.text: Keep it to one course, one community and one service; at most add an accelerated service or a mastermind tier.
principles.quote: But, honestly? Most of the time, one course, one community, and one service is perfect.

principles.text: One of each product forms a natural value ladder; customers only choose how they want to do it.
principles.quote: This means that your customers only have to choose how they want to "do it."

principles.text: Every added option adds a decision point that slows buyers and invites more questions.
principles.quote: Every option you add to your offering creates another decision point for your customer.
